chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Creole origins, French fathers and the quadroon balls
summary: He explains how New Orleans Creole society arose from white fathers, Black mothers, and women hoping for light-skinned daughters.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Isadore Barbarin's father was a Frenchman. Nobody saw him. My grandfather's mother raised him. I don't know what status you would put him in, but his father was a Frenchman who owned a schooner. A schooner just supplies trade between the new basin, like this, over to Mandeville, and they used to bring produce and things from the country out there, the little country towns, into the city to be sold. Spices, herbs, roots, skins, coons,
possums and rabbits, and everything that could get...they'd add some pine. A little small boat.
That's exactly what New Orleans was like, I mean, as far as the mixture of races.
And you're a direct descendant of that. French and Spanish and...

Yeah. And they were descendants of all these people. And there was a whole lot of Chinese came from here. The peculiar thing about New Orleans was that the Whites could pull the hat, or whatever you would call it, with all other women -- everybody's women. But nobody of another race should catch his woman. So this whole Creole business is most times White...

The White and the Black woman. The Black woman was subjected to all kinds of abuse. See, she could be raped, she could be seduced into giving her something, and she'd come up with a child. But generally, they'd never give up their children. See, they don't go too much for orphanage. Whatever the scandal in the family, if it's White man's child, she kept her child...

...by hook or crook. So that's what you see (?). We don't be abandoning' our children, regardless. So you'd get a Black woman with a snow-white child, see. Now, before that, years ago, they had what was called the quadroon balls, where Black women purposely would have a White man to have a White child, because there was something about the gene, that the blacker the woman and a White man, a blond White man, generally you have a blond child or something like that. And these old women knew that. So if you're subject to slavery, so you try to breed something that could help you. So thousands of women had these kids, and you'd have these girls praying for a girl all the time, because they could raise this girl, and this girl, by being White, looking White, she could go into upper strata, out of slavery. There was all kind of ingenious ways (if that's the proper word) to get out of this slavery thing. See, and she could always say she is the maid in the house. Or she says she works for this girl, or she's this girl's gardener, never mentioning that that's her child. And if the girl married White, or with somebody who was similar... There was a whole breed of this thing going, this Creole thing. If she married somebody her color who wasn't White, passing for White they called it, they brought up a breed that brought on the Creole and the free man of color. And you'd see
these Black women in the house there with the Mack (?) or whatever you call it in the house... They had a secret sort of a way.
That's probably where that story Imitation of Life came about.
